articles.abstract: Los regímenes del franco CFA se describen habitualmente como estables porque los dos francos CFA —el franco de la Comunidad Financiera Africana (franc de la Communauté financière africaine) para la UEMOA y el franco de la Cooperación Financiera en África Central (franc de la Coopération financière en Afrique centrale) para la CEMAC— mantienen una paridad fija frente al euro. Este estudio pregunta qué se estabiliza exactamente cuando se tiene en cuenta la evolución de la exposición exterior de la UEMOA y la CEMAC. Distingue la estabilidad nominal bilateral, la estabilidad de los precios internos, la estabilidad efectiva nominal y real, la estabilidad financiera y la credibilidad institucional, pero concentra el análisis empírico en una dimensión: la volatilidad del tipo de cambio efectivo nominal (TCEN). Ngouana (2012) mostró para la UEMOA que, entre 2001 y 2010, el TCEN fue aproximadamente dos veces más volátil bajo el anclaje al euro que bajo un anclaje contrafactual a los derechos especiales de giro (DEG). El estudio realiza una replicación auditada con una convención armonizada de tipos de cambio de fin de mes, amplía el análisis hasta 2024 y aplica el mismo marco a la CEMAC. El universo ampliado de socios se selecciona empíricamente y los intervalos de confianza se obtienen mediante un bootstrap circular de bloques móviles aplicado a series emparejadas. En 2001–2024, el cociente de desviaciones estándar euro/DEG es de 2,00 para la UEMOA y de 3,05 para la CEMAC. Un ejercicio con dos convenciones muestra que el paso de promedios mensuales a observaciones de fin de mes modifica la magnitud del cociente hasta en un 23 por ciento según la zona y la ventana temporal, sin situarlo nunca por debajo de uno. El resultado también resiste pruebas de robustez sobre el predominio del dólar como moneda de facturación y sobre ponderaciones comerciales rezagadas, predeterminadas y fijas. Estos ejercicios siguen siendo contrafactuales contables de equilibrio parcial; no identifican las consecuencias de equilibrio de adoptar otro régimen. Por tanto, los resultados no permiten identificar un ancla óptima. Establecen que la descripción convencional del franco CFA como moneda «estable» se refiere ante todo a su estabilidad nominal bilateral frente al euro y no puede extenderse, sin matices, a la posición exterior multilateral de la moneda.

articles.title: Grandparental Care and Loneliness across Europe: The Role of Cultural Context
articles.authors: Martin Lakomý; Sunwoo Lee; Merril Silverstein
articles.abstract: Loneliness is a phenomenon associated with older age and linked to lower well-being and other adverse outcomes. While the factors contributing to loneliness and potential remedies for its reduction have received growing attention, little consideration has been given to grandchild caregiving as a meaningful and socially integrative activity that may ameliorate loneliness—despite its potential both to constrain social participation and to enhance it. This study examines the association between grandparental caregiving and loneliness, with specific attention to the role of macro-socio-cultural context within Europe. We use data from individuals aged 50–90 participating in the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe. Within-person fixed-effects modeling across five waves reveals a negative association between the intensity of grandparental care and loneliness. Tests across groups of European countries differentiated by their individualistic and collectivistic orientations reveal that grandparental care is associated with lower loneliness in individualistic countries and with higher loneliness in the most collectivistic countries. Results are discussed in terms of the broader social consequences of grandparenting and are interpreted as consistent with the possibility that caregiving is particularly beneficial in contexts where it is experienced as a more voluntary activity.

articles.title: Searching for Radiophobia: Risk framing and nuclear stance in Swedish newspaper editorials and op-eds, 2002–2024
articles.authors: John C. H. Lindberg
articles.abstract: Radiophobia has long featured in debates over nuclear power, but has rarely been examined as a measurable feature of discourse itself. This study investigates whether radiophobia-related language can be identified systematically in Swedish opinion discourse on nuclear power, and whether such language is associated with particular stance positions. Drawing on a corpus of 1,438 opinion and editorial articles published between 2002 and 2024 across six major Swedish newspapers, the study combines manual stance coding with two lexical measures: a Swedish sentiment lexicon capturing general evaluative tone and a theory-driven dictionary designed to identify radiophobia-related framing, including references to contamination, radiation exposure, bodily harm, and accidents. The results show that radiophobia density is strongly associated with anti-nuclear positioning and remains a significant predictor even when general sentiment is controlled for. Anti-nuclear texts also exhibit higher average radiophobia density, more radiophobia-related lexical hits, and higher shares of repeated and high-intensity radiophobia framing than neutral or pro-nuclear texts. The findings suggest that radiophobia-related discourse is not reducible to general negativity, but constitutes a specific risk-oriented repertoire within elite nuclear debate. The study offers an empirical operationalisation of radiophobia as a discursive construct and illustrates the value of theory-driven lexical analysis for studying issue-specific framing in contested policy domains.

articles.title: The Changing Role of Major Stakeholders: A Review of Publisher, Vendor, and Institutional Adaptation in the Scholarly Communication Ecosystem
articles.authors: HAFIZA KINZA GHULAM HUSSAIN
articles.abstract: This article reviews the changing roles of major stakeholders in the scholarly communication ecosystem, focusing on publishers, vendors, and academic institutions. The rapid growth of digital technologies, open access initiatives, and evolving researcher expectations have significantly transformed traditional scholarly communication practices. Through a critical review of existing literature, this study examines how these stakeholders redefine their responsibilities and adopt adaptation strategies to remain relevant in a dynamic academic environment. The analysis highlights key strategies such as business model innovation, service redesign, policy reform, and technological integration as central to effective adaptation. The findings indicate that publishers increasingly function as service providers, vendors play a vital role in technological infrastructure and analytics, and institutions adopt more active roles in research dissemination and support. This review concludes that sustained collaboration and continuous adaptation among publishers, vendors, and institutions are essential for developing an efficient, accessible, and sustainable scholarly communication ecosystem.

articles.title: "Fill Out this Survey": Capabilities and Detection of Agentic Browsers
articles.authors: Renata Topinkova; Carsten Schwemmer
articles.abstract: Researchers increasingly rely on people to produce data through online interfaces. Agentic browsers create a new challenge for these workflows because they can navigate websites and complete tasks on a user’s behalf with little technical knowledge or effort. We evaluate whether three consumer-facing agentic browsers can complete online surveys and whether recently proposed measures can detect or prevent their use. The agents received only one simple instruction, "Fill out this survey", without detailed prompting or technical optimization. We tested technical screening measures, visible and invisible CAPTCHAs, AI-specific prompt-injection checks, consistency across a longer survey, and the completion of several surveys from a single instruction. The agents completed surveys with little or no user input, maintained assigned demographic profiles, and passed all tested prompt-leaking and jailbreak-style checks. Browser metadata did not reveal automated participation, and invisible reCAPTCHA was consistently passed by some browsers. Visible reCAPTCHA created the strongest barrier, although agents could sometimes solve it or return control to the user. These findings show that widely available AI agents can take over tasks intended for human participants while producing responses that appear coherent and plausible. This raises broader questions about how researchers can verify that supposedly human-generated data were actually produced by humans.

articles.title: Public support for climate mitigation and adaptation policies across Europe
articles.authors: Mary Sanford; Žan Mlakar; E. Keith Smith; Thijs Bouman; johannes emmerling; Alessio Levis; Silvia Pianta; Goda Perlaviciute; Lea Stapper; Massimo Tavoni
articles.abstract: Understanding the drivers of public support for climate policies is crucial for designing socially feasible policy packages. However, most large-scale public opinion surveys focus primarily on mitigation policies. Here, we combine two representative survey waves from nine European countries (n = 27,910) to directly compare determinants of public support for climate change mitigation versus adaptation measures. We find that respondents support both mitigation and adaptation as policy objectives, but support specific adaptation policies slightly more than specific mitigation measures. Moreover, support for the two is shaped by a different composition of individual characteristics and policy evaluations. While adaptation support is driven primarily by perceived effectiveness, mitigation support is mostly driven by cost salience and politicisation. Our results suggest a stark difference in how Europeans incorporate the costs and benefits of mitigation versus adaptation policies into their support, and suggest avenues for remedying this imbalance.

articles.title: Selling the Feeling of Being Understood: Trust, Access, and Power in AI's Marketing Turn
articles.authors: Nora Feline Pösl
articles.abstract: In one week in July 2026, three leading AI companies publicly defined themselves through one another. SpaceXAI launched Grok 4.5 through comparative performance claims; Anthropic released the cinematic campaign There's hope in hard questions; and OpenAI's CEO mocked that campaign while relocating competition to price, access, and efficiency. This commentary reads the exchange as a relational repertoire of legitimation rather than as three stable corporate identities. Drawing on archived campaign materials, executive posts, corporate statements, and trade coverage from February to July 2026, it distinguishes registers of trust, access, and founder-centred power. These registers are enabled and constrained, though not mechanically determined, by revenue dependencies. Their common object is the user's relation to AI infrastructure. Anthropic's campaign and accompanying Reflect feature go further by marketing and operationalising the experience of being understood, converting a mechanism associated with sycophancy and affective dependence into a corporate asset and a platform-level mode of user governance.

articles.title: A Machine Learning Approach for Nominative Record Linkage in Chinese Historical Databases
articles.authors: Bruce Yu; Yueran Hou; Yibei Wu; Cameron Campbell
articles.abstract: We introduce a generic machine learning-based pipeline for nominative linkage of records within and across large-scale Chinese historical datasets. The pipeline addresses key challenges, including character variations, incomplete data, and scalability issues specific to historical datasets in which names and other attributes are recorded with Chinese characters, not just for China, but potentially for Korea, Japan and Vietnam. Techniques developed for attributes recorded in phonetic alphabets are of limited usefulness for Chinese characters not only because homonyms are common, but characters that are similar enough in appearance to be frequently mistaken for each other may sound completely different. Our approach integrates stroke-based character embeddings for efficient blocking, supervised classification with active learning for record matching, and graph-based clustering for final linkage. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this pipeline using the career records of officials in the China Government Employee Database-Qing Jinshenlu (CGED-Q JSL) as a test case. We achieve improved linkage quality compared to standard probabilistic methods, with substantially longer linked sequences of career records and fewer aberrant transitions. To validate the generalizability, we also successfully apply the pipeline to another database and a cross-database linkage task. By minimizing the need for manual tuning, our pipeline offers a more accessible and effective solution for Chinese historical data linkage.

articles.title: How Feeling Understood Becomes Reinforcement: Adaptive Resonance in Human-LLM Interaction
articles.authors: Nora Feline Pösl
articles.abstract: Hundreds of millions of users now engage with large language models (LLMs) for advice, emotional support, and ongoing interaction. Existing frameworks capture this dynamic only partially: parasocial theory accounts for attachment without reciprocity, sycophancy research isolates model behavior from interaction dynamics, and echo chamber theory operates at the collective rather than the individual level. This article introduces Adaptive Resonance as a sociological concept that integrates these dimensions into a mechanism-centered account of human-LLM interaction. The mechanism links system adaptation, the user's interpretive experience of being understood, reduced epistemic friction, and behavioral reinforcement into a process that is analytically agnostic with regard to its outcomes — enabling intellectual collaboration in some configurations and producing dependency, ideological reinforcement, or amplification of dysfunctional patterns in others. The article specifies moderating factors, two distinct bonding pathways, and structural conditions of political economy, providing a framework for empirical investigation across vulnerability axes.

articles.title: Inside Algebra Students’ Mathematical Worlds: Insights from Students’ Artworks
articles.authors: Jialu Fan
articles.abstract: Since the late 1990s, many U.S. states have responded to the Algebra for All initiative by providing students with equal and early access to algebra. Despite the policy successfully increasing access, urban districts nationwide have continued to experience alarming algebra failure rates over the past two decades, with Minnesota the only state still mandating eighth-grade algebra. In this critical moment, there is a pressing need to better understand students’ experiences in algebra classrooms. Yet children—especially those from historically underserved groups—are often underrepresented as contributors to knowledge in educational research in general, and specifically in mathematics education. Using arts-based research methods, this study uncovers the mathematics identities of historically underserved students (N=12) in North Minneapolis. Findings highlight students’ emotional tensions as algebra learners living precarious lives, as well as their visions of an algebra classroom that supports their overall wellbeing. By interpreting students’ often-hidden experiences as algebra learners, this work offers theoretical and methodological implications for including children as research contributors, as well as insights that can inform pedagogical practices in eighth-grade algebra.

articles.title: PLACING ACCESSIBILITY AT THE CENTER OF TRAVEL BEHAVIOR MODELING: A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK
articles.authors: Matheus Fontenelle Siqueira; Carlos Felipe Grangeiro Loureiro
articles.abstract: The paradigm shift from mobility to accessibility planning demands analytical approaches to understanding and modeling travel behavior. Yet most behavioral frameworks still lack a clearer representation of how urban form, individual, accessibility, and travel behavior relate to each other; most represent accessibility indirectly through exogenous attributes of the built environment and transport networks, neglecting its temporal, individual and digital components. This paper proposes a conceptual framework that positions accessibility as the central mediator between urban structure and individual travel decisions. Grounded in time geography and building on the multidimensional accessibility model of Geurs and van Wee (2004, 2026), the framework integrates land-use, transport, temporal, individual-and-social, and digital components, and articulates how tangible constraints and perceptions jointly shape travel behavior. The framework is designed to accommodate feedback loops and self-selection mechanisms, providing a structure for both theoretical reflection and empirical analysis. As a proof of concept, we apply it through a multigroup Structural Equation Model to household travel survey data from Fortaleza, Brazil, a highly segregated metropolis. The empirical results support the mediating role of accessibility and reveal gendered differences in how its components translate into motorized and non-motorized mobility. By making explicit the influences of accessibility components on travel behavior, the framework offers researchers and planners a structured basis for hypothesis formulation and for aligning transport modeling with goals of social inclusion, accessibility equity, and sustainable urban development.

articles.title: AVID Insights: Diverse Paths to College Predisposition and Search
articles.authors: Brian Holzman; Aminah Crawford; Kristian Edosomwan
articles.abstract: AVID is a college access program for students in the “academic middle,” particularly those from socioeconomically and racially marginalized backgrounds. Although research has examined AVID’s association with college enrollment, less is known about its relationship with earlier stages of the college-choice process. Using nationally representative HSLS data, we examine whether AVID participation is associated with students’ expectations of earning a bachelor’s and engagement in key college search activities. We also assess whether these associations vary by race/ethnicity, first-generation status, and family poverty level. AVID participation is positively associated with attending college programs or tours and consulting school counselors. In some cases, these associations are stronger among socioeconomically and racially marginalized students, suggesting AVID may help reduce disparities in access to college information and guidance.

articles.title: Metodología para la preparación de la documentación técnica de proyectos de I+D+i ante auditorías de beneficios tributarios
articles.authors: Sebastian Iglesias-Osores
articles.abstract: Este documento fija una metodología para estructurar la documentación técnica de un proyecto de investigación, desarrollo tecnológico e innovación (I+D+i) de modo que resista la doble revisión que hoy pesa sobre el beneficio tributario: la fiscalización técnica de la ejecución, a cargo del CONCYTEC, y la fiscalización tributaria del gasto, a cargo de la SUNAT. La lógica de fondo es sencilla: un criterio o una partida que no cuenta con un documento fechado que la respalde no existe para el auditor.

articles.title: La vida breve de los derechos: Séneca, la prescripción y el arte de no llegar tarde en el Derecho civil chileno (a propósito del De Brevitate Vitae)
articles.authors: Andrés Gabriel Varas Quijón
articles.abstract: Hacia el año 49, Séneca escribió a Paulino el diagnóstico más citado de la filosofía del tiempo: no recibimos una vida breve; la hacemos breve —«non accipimus brevem vitam, sed fecimus»—, porque la desperdiciamos viviendo «como si fuéramos a vivir siempre» y aplazando lo importante para una edad a la que pocos llegan. Este trabajo sostiene una tesis simple y, hasta donde se ve, no explorada con esta frontalidad: el Derecho civil chileno tiene su propio De Brevitate Vitae, y se llama prescripción extintiva. La lógica es idéntica: los derechos, como la vida, no mueren por breves; mueren por no usarse. El artículo 2492 del Código Civil define la institución por la inercia —«no haberse ejercido dichas acciones y derechos durante cierto lapso de tiempo»—; el artículo 2514 pone a correr el reloj «desde que la obligación se haya hecho exigible»; y el 2515 fija la regla general que todo titular debiera tatuarse: tres años las acciones ejecutivas, cinco las ordinarias. El trabajo recorre la arquitectura completa con mirada senequiana y utilidad de trinchera: el brocardo que traduce al foro la moraleja del filósofo —el Derecho socorre a los que velan, no a los que duermen—; el muestrario de plazos breves que matan derechos por descuido (los dos años de los honorarios profesionales, los seis meses de la redhibitoria de muebles, el año de las acciones posesorias); las pausas del reloj —interrupción por demanda judicial o reconocimiento del deudor, suspensión, renuncia solo del plazo cumplido y necesidad de alegación—; la otra cara de la moneda —la prescripción adquisitiva, donde el mismo tiempo que castiga al que duerme premia al que actúa—; y la tendencia comparada que le da a Séneca la victoria legislativa: el mundo entero está encogiendo sus plazos, y Francia pasó de treinta años a cinco. Se cierra con las reglas prácticas del litigante que no llega tarde y con la traducción jurídica del consuelo estoico: vita, si uti scias, longa est —los derechos duran lo suficiente para quien los ejerce—.

articles.title: From Traditional Shamanism to the "Esoteric Call Center": Socioeconomic Dynamics and Transnationalization of Esoteric Services in the Laboyos (Pitalito, Colombia)
articles.authors: Luis Felipe Narvaez Galindez
articles.abstract: This article analyzes the emergence and consolidation of Pitalito (Laboyos Valley, Colombia) as a transnational epicenter for digital witchcraft services. Through a socio-anthropological approach, it examines how the anxieties of the "risk society" (Ulrich Beck) and "liquid modernity" (Zygmunt Bauman) create a persistent demand for magical solutions in the face of emotional and professional uncertainty. The study describes the praxis of the "Esoteric Call Center," a business model that adapts traditional rituals to the logic of the "network society" (Manuel Castells), transforming the social function of witchcraft into a consumer product. It is argued that while the symbolic structure of magic remains, its purpose is reconfigured towards profit, altering its ethical framework. Finally, the key factors for Pitalito's success—linguistic capital, a technical-commercial ecosystem, and cultural heritage—are identified, and the future of this service economy is discussed at the crossroads of economic innovation and social tolerance.

articles.title: ¿Quién puede hablar sobre inteligencia artificial? Género, poder y discurso mediático / Who Can Speak about Artificial Intelligence? Gender, Power, and Media Discourse
articles.authors: Maider Eizmendi-Iraola; Simón Peña-Fernández
articles.abstract:
[ES] En los últimos años, el interés mediático por la inteligencia artificial (IA) ha crecido de forma exponencial, impulsando debates sobre sus aplicaciones, beneficios y riesgos. En este contexto, las fuentes expertas desempeñan un papel clave en la construcción del discurso informativo. Este artículo examina la cobertura mediática de la IA desde una perspectiva de género, con especial atención a las fuentes utilizadas. Para ello, se analizan las piezas periodísticas publicadas durante los primeros seis meses de 2025 en las ediciones digitales de El País y El Mundo que incluyen en su titular los términos “Inteligencia Artificial” o “IA”, identificando un total de 529 fuentes personales. Los resultados evidencian una notable asimetría de género en la selección de fuentes, pues las mujeres representan el 26,84% del total. Asimismo, se observa una clara segregación horizontal en función de la temática y del rol asignado. Esta infrarrepresentación femenina puede influir tanto en la manera en que se abordan cuestiones clave como en la construcción del imaginario sobre qué actores poseen legitimidad para intervenir en el debate público. En este sentido, la incorporación de voces diversas no solo responde a un principio de equidad, sino que también resulta fundamental para enriquecer la calidad y pluralidad del debate en torno a la IA.

[EN] In recent years, media interest in artificial intelligence (AI) has grown exponentially, fueling debates about its applications, benefits, and risks. In this context, expert sources play a key role in shaping the news narrative. This article examines media coverage of AI from a gender perspective, paying particular attention to the sources used. To this end, it analyzes news articles published during the first six months of 2025 in the digital editions of El País and El Mundo that include the terms "Artificial Intelligence" or "AI" in their headlines, identifying a total of 529 personal sources. The results reveal a significant gender imbalance in source selection: women represent, on average, 26.84% of the total. Furthermore, a clear horizontal segregation is observed based on the topic and the assigned role. This underrepresentation of women can influence both how key issues are addressed and the construction of perceptions about which actors have the legitimacy to participate in the public debate. In this sense, the incorporation of diverse voices not only responds to a principle of equity, but is also fundamental to enriching the quality and plurality of the debate surrounding IA.

articles.title: Next-Generation Mortality Forecasting with Deep Learning
articles.authors: Paige Park
articles.abstract: Deep learning is transforming fields like chemistry, engineering, and medicine, but its application to social science fields like demography remains limited. This study explores deep learning as an emerging approach to mortality forecasting, a core area in demographic research. This paper addresses why and how deep learning performs better than three well-known baselines for mortality forecasting. First, it explores the relationship between model architecture and data pooling. Second, it provides a detailed country-level performance analysis, identifying contexts where deep learning underperforms and exploring possible remedies. Third, it discusses the broader applicability and potential of deep learning methods in demography. The findings underscore the potential of deep learning to enhance demographic forecasting and invite broader reflection on the role of computational and AI-driven methods in population studies.

articles.title: Why Do Educational Success Narratives Continue to Organize Schools as Their Practical Efficacy Erodes?
articles.authors: Vance Byun
articles.abstract:
This article examines why an educational success narrative whose practical efficacy has become increasingly unstable continues to organize schools during the college-admissions period, and why the same school structure is experienced by students as different forms of suffering. Narrative is defined here as a form of practical knowledge that links an account of what constitutes a good life, prescriptions for what one must do to attain it, and a causal understanding of why the prescribed path is expected to work. When a narrative organizes repeated practices, it becomes objectified in the allocation of school time, assessment, college counseling, recognition, and resources. Yet the collective practices organized by the narrative, together with broader social change, may erode the very conditions on which the narrative rests. The efficacy of the path may therefore begin to falter while the norms and institutions built around it persist for much longer.

Using college-admissions-centered schooling as a heuristic case, the article analyzes this desynchronization and assembles the dimensions differentiated through the argument—temporal lag, internalization, institutional distribution, narrative quality, and the conditions of survival, performance, and exit—into a V-Q-C coordinate framework. It then derives five mechanisms from different configurations of these dimensions: suffering internal to the narrative, the double bind, anomic suffering, structural compulsion, and guilt produced by attacks on legitimacy.

Finally, the article redefines the task of schooling not as training students in the resilience to endure every form of friction, but as Bildung: the joint cultivation of the capacities and conditions required to interpret the character of friction and to revise, suspend, or exit a given path. Korean schools may teach diverse forms of knowledge while still reducing legitimate life paths to the college-admissions track. Educational pluralism should therefore be assessed not only by the number of subjects taught, but also by the distribution of time, security, recognition, and reversibility that enables students to genuinely test different forms of life.

articles.title: Americans Favor Predistributive Over Redistributive Economic Policies
articles.authors: David Broska; Jonne Kamphorst; Robb Willer
articles.abstract: Redistributive policies designed to reduce economic inequality through taxes and transfers (e.g., safety-net benefits funded by progressive taxation) receive less support in the U.S. than in many Western democracies. Recent work suggests Americans may be more receptive to “predistributive” policies, which seek to reduce economic inequality before taxes and transfers (e.g., minimum-wage increases). Yet existing evidence leaves open whether this support gap characterizes contemporary Americans overall, and whether it persists when the same policy proposals are described in predistributive versus redistributive terms, with their core provisions held constant. Across 31 nationally representative U.S. survey waves fielded from 2015 to 2024 (total N=384,248), we find greater support for policies classified as predistributive than redistributive. We then fielded a preregistered experiment with a national U.S. sample (N=1,009), randomly varying whether otherwise identical policy proposals were described as increasing earnings for people lower in the income distribution, shifting resources from higher- to lower-income individuals, or presented only with the brief policy description given in all conditions. Support was higher under predistributive than redistributive descriptions. Comparison with the control condition clarifies this difference: predistributive descriptions received support comparable to control, whereas redistributive descriptions received lower support. Exploratory analyses suggest perceived respect for hard work and deservingness of beneficiaries were associated with the support gap. Together, these results suggest Americans prefer policies that reduce inequality by influencing earnings more than through taxes and transfers.

articles.title: A Certification Gate for Emerging-Topic Detection: Pre-Registration, Negative Controls, and a Second-Domain Transfer Test on arXiv
articles.authors: Ben-Nicholas Borowski
articles.abstract: Methods for detecting emerging research topics keep multiplying, but they are rarely validated against ground truth chosen independently of the method: most are assessed on internal coherence or a few hand-picked success stories. This paper contributes not a new detector but a certification gate, a pre-registered, negative-controlled validation protocol any emergence detector can be run through. Before results are seen, the gate fixes (i) a binary "flagged rising" criterion, (ii) an externally-sourced positive set and a matched negative-control set, and (iii) Wilson-95% reporting of recall, specificity and precision. Applied to the temporal component of a five-dimension emergence system over arXiv stat.ML (2018–2023; 76 topics), the gate yields recall 93% (14/15, Wilson 95% [70,99]) and specificity 100% (13/13, [77,100]). The identical protocol is then run on a second, structurally different domain (arXiv cs.CR; 2018–2023; 129 topics) under a benchmark frozen and timestamped before scoring. This is a transfer test, not a replication: with only two domains it characterises how the protocol behaves out-of-corpus, not whether the first result reproduces. Recall falls to 62% (10/16, [39,82]) and specificity to 69% (9/13, [42,87]); pooled, recall is 77% (24/31, [60,89]) and specificity 85% (22/26, [66,94]). The intervals are wide by construction: at these n the benchmark is underpowered to rank detectors and demonstrates only the gate. The honest degradation is the point: a validation that reported 100% on one corpus and hid the second would be the overfitting it claims to detect. The protocol, both benchmarks with timestamp proofs, and a disclosed pre-scoring amendment are released, and the gate's numbers are reported with and without that amendment.

articles.title: The Weight of Precedent: Parties, Trust, and Executive Norms
articles.authors: Daniel A. N. Goldstein; Collin Thomas Schumock
articles.abstract: Political executives often adhere to traditions set by their predecessors that establish expected behavior, such as informal limits to their power. However, it remains a puzzle why executives follow norms, which lack legal backing, when they face incentives to violate them. To address this question, we analyze an infinite-horizon formal model incorporating within-party and across-party dynamics to examine when informal constraints on executives persist or collapse. Norm survival hinges on an executive's willingness to transgress a norm and their party condoning this act. The driving mechanism is coordination: violating a norm degrades cooperation between the executive and their party. We also show that the same conditions can support a high-trust equilibrium among parties in which norms survive and a low-trust equilibrium of preemptive violation. Trust-driven collapse is greatest under balanced party competition. The model classifies executive norms by fragility and traces the life cycle of the American presidential two-term tradition.

articles.title: Certification, Not Transformation: The Performance Signature of Italy's Innovative-Firm Status and Its Regional Contingency
articles.authors: Angelo Leogrande; Mauro di Molfetta; Valeria Nortarnicola; Maria Giovanna Trotta; Nicola Magaletti
articles.abstract: Italy's special legal status for "innovative" small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) grants fiscal, financial and administrative benefits intended to strengthen competitiveness, yet whether the status marks a distinctive profile of realised firm performance remains empirically underexplored. Using ten years of balance-sheet data assembled within the LUCE (LUtech Campus Ecosystem) research project on 4,043 firms (2,873 innovative and 1,170 ordinary), we compare the two populations across six performance dimensions—performance persistence, revenue growth, labour productivity, operating profitability, earnings volatility and financial stability. Because the populations differ systematically in size, sector and location, we use propensity-score matching (1,031 balanced pairs) and interpret the resulting differential as a conditional innovative-status premium rather than as a causal effect. Innovative SMEs display a large and robust revenue-growth premium—a median growth rate roughly three-and-a-half times that of matched ordinary peers (+17.3 percentage points per year; rank-biserial 0.53)—coexisting with a fragility penalty of higher earnings volatility and lower financial stability; operating profitability is higher but does not survive our robustness battery, and labour productivity is marginally lower. A within-firm event study around the registration date shows that the growth advantage largely predates registration, indicating that the status certifies and renders visible already-dynamic firms rather than causally upgrading them. The premium is strongly and significantly heterogeneous across space—broadest in the South, where local institutions are weakest—consistent with an institutional-substitution boundary condition that a formal region-by-status interaction confirms. The results are robust to nine alternative estimators, multiple-testing correction and hidden-bias diagnostics. We read the innovative-firm register as an informative screening and monitoring device rather than as a policy whose causal returns we measure.

articles.title: Segment and Rule: Modern Censorship in Authoritarian Regimes
articles.authors: Kun Heo; Antoine Zerbini
articles.abstract: We analyze the incentives of authoritarian regimes to segment access to censored content through technology. Citizens choose whether to pay to access censored online content at a cost fixed by the regime: the firewall. A low firewall segments access and generates more compliance than full censorship - a high firewall - ever could. Regime opponents self-select into consuming censored content, and comply conditional on positive independent reporting. Regime supporters exclusively consume state propaganda, which secures their compliance. This segment-and-rule strategy can be engineered by making local news outlets uninformative, or by affecting the intrinsic benefit from access.

articles.title: Off the Streets: Full-Time Schooling and  Property Crime in São Paulo
articles.authors: Augusto Alves; Bruno Pantaleão; Alei Santos
articles.abstract: The relationship between schooling and crime is well documented in the economics literature: more schooling means less crime. Yet the mechanisms behind this relationship remain an open question, especially in developing countries. We ask whether full-time schooling lowers crime by building human capital or simply by keeping students supervised, exploiting the staggered rollout of São Paulo's Full-Time Education Program (\emph{Programa de Ensino Integral}) across public schools between 2012 and 2024. Using \citet{callaway2021difference}'s doubly-robust difference-in-differences estimator applied to geocoded crime records, we find that adopting the full-time model reduces property crime in the surrounding area by about 7\% (18.8 fewer offenses per hexagon-year), an effect driven by robbery. The reductions are sharply concentrated in time and by offender: theft falls by 26\% during school hours but is, if anything, slightly higher outside them; effects are strongest on school days; and crimes committed by juveniles fall disproportionately --- roughly 65\% for theft and 23\% for robbery. Because the effects emerge precisely when, and for whom, school supervision is most binding, they are hard to reconcile with longer-run human-capital or opportunity-cost channels and instead point to incapacitation. Full-time schooling thus yields immediate public-safety gains in a middle-income setting, which is relevant to both education and crime-prevention policy.

articles.title: Reconstructing Sexual Economy: The role of Women in the subsistence of Sex Work and Tourism and the Rise of Single Mothers in The Philippines
articles.authors: Rohit Chowdhury
articles.abstract: This paper examines the Philippine sexual economy through a structural sociological and historical lens, arguing that commercial sex work is not merely an outcome of individual choice or moral failure but a rational adaptation to intersecting historical, economic, and institutional constraints. Drawing upon interdisciplinary literature from sociology, history, gender studies, public policy, and human rights, the study traces the evolution of the Philippine sexual economy from Spanish colonial rule and the institutionalization of prostitution around American military bases to its contemporary integration within global tourism. It demonstrates how persistent poverty, gender-segmented labor markets, discriminatory employment practices, and inadequate social welfare systems have made sex work a significant strategy of female household subsistence. The paper further examines how these structural conditions contribute to the growth of solo motherhood and the enduring marginalization of Amerasian children abandoned by foreign military personnel and tourists. It argues that the coexistence of criminalization, anti-trafficking legislation, and external geopolitical influence has produced a policy framework that simultaneously punishes, victimizes, and silences sex workers while denying them labor rights and limiting effective public health interventions. Rather than framing prostitution solely as a criminal justice or moral issue, the analysis situates it within broader systems of political economy, gender inequality, and postcolonial governance. The paper concludes by proposing evidence-based structural reforms, including labor market expansion, strengthened support for solo mothers, rights-based legal reform, and greater accountability for the historical legacies of foreign military intervention. By reframing the Philippine sexual economy as a structural rather than individual phenomenon, this study contributes to broader debates on gender, labor, postcolonial development, and the sociology of informal economies.

articles.title: ‘Do No (Further) Harm’ Ethics Guidelines for Migrant Disaster Victim Identification (MDVI)
articles.authors: Valentina Azarova; Geoff Boyce; Noemi Magugliani; Álvaro Ramírez-March
articles.abstract:
The DVI framework, conceived and regulated by the INTERPOL Working Group, provides guidelines to intervene in catastrophic situations that result in “an unexpected death of many people”. This understanding of disasters frames the causes of death as unusual, unanticipated, and temporally limited. Yet, the deaths of persons crossing borders, especially those crossing in ways that have been illegalised, and the reality of migrants ‘going missing’ on their journey to Europe have become both routine and a predictable consequence of border securitisation and of state authorities’ deterrence policies and strategies. Indeed, there is extensive scientific research demonstrating that the causes and reasons for migrant deaths and disappearances are largely structural and systemic, made up of social, economic and political policies and institutions.

For these reasons, MDVI includes challenges that are different from ‘traditional’ DVI events. These are not limited to scientific or technical challenges—which include, for example, the fact that “many of the accepted methods of identification (DNA; fingerprints; dental) are often inappropriate or even impossible, due to legal obstacles and socioeconomic conditions of the countries of origin and the resulting lack of regular dental treatment, fingerprint resources and family records.” Rather, some of the unique challenges associated with MDVI are structural, arising from both politics and policy.

Whilst most technical challenges (and some political ones) have been acknowledged, it must also be acknowledged that the causes of migrant deaths and disappearances are integrally linked with ongoing policies and practices willfully enacted by state authorities to control borders, and systemically deficient state responses to such unlawful acts. In absence of a clear, contextualised safeguarding structure alive to the specificities of ‘migrant disasters’, any steps or interventions taken under the umbrella of MDVI with the intention to improve identification procedures may in fact contribute to further harm—including against the dead and their loved ones, others on the move, and/or support groups. Such harm from identification procedures risks contributing to additional death and disappearance caused by harmful border control policies, and the failure to hold state actions to account.

These guiding principles aim to help state-led DVI processes in the migration context adequately account and respond to this potential for ongoing and further harm. The principles build and elaborate on the ethical guidelines that already bind forensic and medical professionals as communities of practice, while seeking to integrate critical reflections on harm arising from lived experiences of border/ing violence and family accompaniment.

articles.title: "Even in poverty, a Jew is a prince": The press coverage of the deaths of Beitar movement commanders in Eretz Israel
articles.authors: Barak Bar-Zohar
articles.abstract:
This qualitative textual analysis examines the journalistic coverage of the deaths of six former Beitar Movement commanders in the land of Israel: Shimshon Unichman (1961), Menachem Arber (1961), Eri Jabotinsky (1969), Binyamin Eliav (1974), Yonah Froehlich (1976) and Moshe Gold (1986), as reported in thirteen Hebraic newspapers. This line of inquiry reveals that while the deaths of these men constituted as notable media events in the revisionist party press, competing daily newspapers relegated the news to the margins, with rather informative, albeit respectful, mentions. Furthermore, the extent of each figure’s integration into Israeli public or political life after their term as Beitar commanders, as well as Eri Jabotinsky’s family lineage, significantly influenced the scope and tone of media coverage.
Between the lines, this article also points to the early decline of the political-propaganda press, which often presented a one-dimensional worldvie. In practice, the Israeli press covered the deaths of former Beitar commanders in an informative and respectful manner, portraying them as national pioneers. Even more so, the revisionist press framed them as folk heroes (Unichman), as spokesmen for Ze’ev Jabotinsky (Arber) and as a source of personal and collective pride (Eri Jabotinsky). Coverage of the deaths of Eliav, Froehlich and Gold, however, was considerably more limited due to the closure of revisionist newspapers, Eliav’s ideological distancing from the political right, and Froehlich’s and Gold’s withdrawal from the political and public arenas. At the same time, and without exception, the journalistic coverage emphasized the Beitar ethos of courage, splendor and righteousness of cause.

articles.title: LA ZONA DEL FRANCO CFA: EL CALLEJÓN SIN SALIDA - La decisión que nadie quiere asumir
articles.authors: Armand Salouo-Mvondo
articles.abstract: ¿Por qué persiste la zona del franco CFA pese al creciente cuestionamiento y a reformas parciales que no han alterado su arquitectura esencial? Este documento de trabajo sostiene que la continuidad del sistema no se explica ni por su desempeño técnico por sí solo ni por una voluntad unilateral de Francia de conservarlo. Es el resultado de la convergencia silenciosa de múltiples racionalidades individuales —francesas, africanas, institucionales y privadas—, ninguna de las cuales está dispuesta a asumir por sí sola el coste de la decisión que aclararía el futuro del sistema. Cada actor capaz de transformar la zona del franco CFA tiene razones estructurales para no hacerlo. Esta convergencia no coordinada produce una no decisión estructural que tiende a afianzarse. La reforma de la UEMOA de 2021, la presión de la Alianza de Estados del Sahel y la aprobación de la CEMAC Act por el Congreso de Estados Unidos en 2025 han reconfigurado el sistema de restricciones sin resolver la cuestión fundamental y, con ello, han abierto una brecha en la frontera que tradicionalmente separaba a defensores y detractores de este vestigio de la era colonial. Este documento de trabajo procede de un libro de próxima publicación: Zone franc : l’impasse (Kurukan Publishing, Yaundé, 2026).

articles.title: Socio-structural and personal components of studying: How social background and  personality shape aspirations and transition
articles.authors: Jessica Ordemann; Michael Becker
articles.abstract: Does the personal component of aspiration add to social background’s effects on the transition to study? Often neglected in research, our study examines the interplay between personal (Big Five) and socio-structural components of aspirations at the transition to higher education. Drawing on a large-scale longitudinal German study, the National Educational Panel Study, NEPS, we analyse impact of a student’s personality in grade 9 on their aspirations in grade 11 and the transition to study after graduating with a higher education entrance certificate of 4042 students including 1667 from non-academic families. We employ logistic regression analysis followed by average marginal effects (AME). Findings show that—beyond social origin—aspirations encompass a personality component which independently impacts the transition to studying; even when adjusted for achievement differences. We find an overall effect of openness, but its effect is largely driven by non-academic students. Our study therefore highlights the importance of including both social and psychological perspectives when researching topics of inequality.

articles.title: The Precarious Center: Structural Vulnerability and the Economic Squeeze of South Asia’s Lower Middle Class
articles.authors: Rohit Chowdhury
articles.abstract: This paper examines the lower middle class in South Asia as a structurally vulnerable “missing middle” caught between extreme poverty and genuine income security. It argues that conventional middle-class definitions often obscure the fragility of households that earn too much to qualify for targeted welfare yet too little to access private health care, quality education, or reliable financial protection. Drawing on evidence from India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and West Bengal, the paper shows how this group is squeezed by informal employment, exclusion from social protection, catastrophic out-of-pocket health costs, rising education expenses, regressive taxation, inflation, and debt dependence. It also highlights how remittances, asset ownership, and consumer goods can create a false impression of security while masking deep exposure to economic shocks. The paper concludes that although the extreme poor remain the most deprived in absolute terms, the lower middle class is arguably the most systemically neglected and precariously positioned segment in South Asia, trapped in a cycle of permanent vulnerability without a stable path to upward mobility.

articles.title: Equal Protection or Conceptual Conformity? Global Gender Governance, Norm Translation and Cultural Sovereignty
articles.authors: Sixbert Sangwa
articles.abstract: Global gender governance has expanded from instruments centred on women’s legal equality and protection from sex-based discrimination to a heterogeneous field encompassing gender mainstreaming, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, sexuality education, institutional inclusion and gender-transformative programming. This article asks when such expansion represents legitimate human-rights protection and when transnational norm transfer risks becoming conceptual conformity. It combines a critical integrative review of 42 scholarly works with structured analysis of 29 primary policy instruments issued by global, regional and national institutions. Searches were conducted through five pre-specified OpenAlex queries and reported using a PRISMA-adapted, transparently bounded design. The analysis distinguishes a universal protection floor, context-dependent institutional measures and contested anthropological propositions. It finds no evidence of a single, centrally coordinated global command structure. It does identify polycentric conceptual expansion, soft-law diffusion, donor and reputational leverage, and forms of localisation whose practical openness varies considerably. Global norms have provided indispensable resources against violence, exclusion and sex-based inequality; they can also blur the boundary between protecting persons and requiring assent to disputed accounts of sex, identity, embodiment and family. The article develops a fifteen-test Conceptual Sovereignty and Gender Governance Framework to assess dignity, safety, evidence, authority, participation, translation, non-compulsion, proportionality, women’s rights, minority protection, conscience, democratic legitimacy, conditionality and reviewability. Equal dignity, it argues, requires robust protection without making conceptual uniformity the price of civic inclusion.

articles.title: Value Determinants of Youth Professional Self-Realization (Author's English Translation)
articles.authors: Inna Gazieva
articles.abstract:
The article is devoted to the theoretical and empirical analysis of the professional self-realization of students and the definition of its value determinants. According to the author, the professional self-realization of young people is a stage of socialization, where professional potential is formed and realized; it includes a set of professional competencies and special personality traits necessary for the effective implementation of labor activity. Professional self-realization is impossible without the creation of appropriate conditions, which is part of the State Youth Personnel Policy: an institutionally organized socio-managerial activity of the subjects of youth policy aimed at regulating personnel processes in the youth environment of the country.

The effectiveness of the organization of personnel processes depends on how much this process responds to the values of youth.

To determine the value conditions for the professional self-realization of students, the results of a sociological study were analyzed. The study was conducted in 2022 under the guidance of the author among Russian students (N=18,392). As a result of the analysis, two groups of value determinants of professional self-realization were identified: primary and secondary.

Primary value determinants are strategic; they should be considered when building the personnel policy of the organization, and they are in the area of responsibility of the head of the organization; this group includes the value conditions through which respondents reveal the content of self-realization.

Secondary value determinants of professional self-realization are tactical. They should form the basis of the adaptation practice for each new employee of the organization and be in the area of responsibility of the immediate supervisor; this group includes the most important value conditions in employment for students who need the opportunity for professional self-realization.

The revealed value determinants of professional self-realization can be included in the program of adaptation of young specialists in the organization.

articles.title: ProtoHomo extinction, Homo sapiens' Levantine birth, and DNA-driven ProgRetrogProg Evolution
articles.authors: Şahin ÇAKIR
articles.abstract:
There is no consensus on the term “human”: All hominins? The genus Homo? Anatomically modern-like humans only? None of them. In New Paradigm:
1) “Human” or Homo sapiens (incl. initial Neanderthals and initial Denisovans) originated from the Levantine macroevolution ~140 ka (thousand years) ago. In other words, the Last Common Ancestor of them was NOT  before 500 ka. 
2) Pre-140 ka Homo was an unknown extinct taxon Proto-Human (ProtoHomo). The evidence presented here confirms that the glacial maximum ~140 ka ago largely wiped them out (incl. Pseudo-Sapiens, Pseudo-Neanderthals, Pseudo-Denisovans, and Homo luzonensis except the last Javanese H. erectus).
3) The relationships shown here between global overheatings and anatomical progressions (and vice versa) reveal that DNA (genetic program) has driven fluctuating human evolution (ProgRetrogProg or RetrogProgRetrogProg evolution). This fluctuation implies the existence of two opposing forces within the DNA and their unending struggle for dominance. The evidence also suggests that behavioral and cognitive fluctuations, too, may have been DNA-driven.

articles.title: The Politics of Conscription in Northern Ireland, 1938-1946
articles.authors: Connor T. Jerzak
articles.abstract: This article examines how wartime debates over the possible introduction of military conscription reshaped conceptions of citizenship and political authority in Northern Ireland between 1938 – 1946. Drawing on primary documents from Northern Ireland, Éire, and Great Britain, it traces how Unionists initially championed conscription as a way to affirm equal status with Britain, even as they upheld internal hierarchies that disadvantaged Catholics. Yet divisions within Unionist ranks—exacerbated by British reluctance to enforce conscription—challenged long-standing assumptions of Protestant “loyalty” and Catholic “disloyalty.” At the same time, Nationalists framed conscription as an illegitimate imposition by a foreign state, underscoring their self-identification as Irish citizens under occupation. Perhaps paradoxically, by forgoing conscription, Britain gained a measure of legitimacy in Catholic eyes, encouraging some Nationalists to engage more constructively with British institutions and signaling new possibilities for political accommodation. In revealing these wartime dynamics, this analysis highlights how the conscription controversy helped recalibrate citizenship, unsettle entrenched power structures, and broaden the political landscape in Northern Ireland.

articles.title: Social Environment as a Factor in the Changing Values of Student Youth (Author's English Translation)
articles.authors: Inna Gazieva
articles.abstract:
This article is devoted to the study of the influence of the social environment and its changes on the values of students. The article says that ensuring adherence to values is a difficult task, including a deep study of the nature of values, the conditions for their formation, as well as the development of measures to ensure sustainable adherence to these values, especially among students. Based on various definitions of values, the article presents the author's operational definition, which became the starting point for the organization of applied sociological research. Based on the conducted factorial and cluster analysis of the sociological research data, typological groups were formed, described through correlation with the heroes of Russian literature. Thanks to the chosen method of typological analysis, it was possible to clearly demonstrate possible changes in the values of student youth under the influence of a changing social environment, and also to describe the likely social trajectories of students as a result of moving away from previous values.

Author's English translation of the article published in Russian: Higher Education in Russia (Vysshee obrazovanie v Rossii), 2024, vol. 33, no. 2, pp. 54-72. DOI: 10.31992/0869-3617-2024-33-2-54-72. The Russian original is the version of record. Archived translation: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21610437

articles.title: An Empirical Model for the Analysis of Social Values of Student Youth (Author's English Translation)
articles.authors: Inna Gazieva
articles.abstract:
Introduction. The topic of values in general, as well as the problem of their study in particular, is gaining increasing popularity in modern Russian discourse, which is explained by the significant acceleration of social changes mediated by geopolitical and domestic political processes, as well as by the updated framework of legal regulation: strengthening the integration into public life of traditional Russian values, enshrined by Decree of the President of the Russian Federation of 09.11.2022 No. 809 "On the Approval of the Fundamentals of State Policy for the Preservation and Strengthening of Traditional Russian Spiritual and Moral Values." This state of affairs suggests the need for a sociological diagnosis of the value space of modern Russian society.

Aim. Today there are many tools for studying values, but most of them are aimed at assessing individual values, while we are interested in social values, which determined the purpose of the article: to develop and describe an empirical model for analyzing social values, which is based on the idea of the need to use a set of indicators for their cumulative assessment.

Methods. The indicators of the assessment of social values identified by the author include: value relations, value preferences, value attitudes, value actions. On the basis of the proposed approach, a sociological toolkit has been developed, which has been tested in the course of diagnosing the value space of student youth. The survey was conducted from May 17 to June 1, 2023 (N=4338).

Results. The results of testing the empirical model of the analysis of social values demonstrated a pronounced disparity in the respondents' attitude to the proposed indicators of their measurement, which is explained by the presence of a noticeable gap between the understanding of the ideal idea of values and actual adherence to them.

Conclusions. The tested empirical model of the analysis of social values can form the basis for studying social values not only of other socio-demographic groups, but also of Russian society as a whole.

Author's English translation of the article published in Russian: State and Municipal Management. Scholar Notes, 2025, no. 2, pp. 230-240. EDN: VRZLPQ. The Russian original is the version of record. Archived translation: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21610439

articles.title: Patriotism as a Social Value: The Perception of Student Youth (Author's English Translation)
articles.authors: Inna Gazieva
articles.abstract:
The article addresses an urgent problem in the study and organization of youth policy: the assessment and formation of the value of patriotism. Current political rhetoric often speaks of a record-high level of patriotism in Russian society, including among students, but a closer study of the social environment shows that such statements are somewhat declarative. Accordingly, the aim of this article is to determine the content of the concept of patriotism as a value, which formed the basis of the methodology of the author's sociological research on the formation of social values among students. The survey was conducted from 17 May to 1 June 2023 through the personal accounts of full-time RANEPA students (N=4338). Based on factor and cluster analysis of the data, a factor of the value of patriotism was formed, and typological groups of respondents were described according to the distribution of cluster-center coordinates and the analysis of the judgments constituting the patriotism factor. The group in the zone of positive factor values is called "social humanists": they highly value patriotism, are ready to support and develop their country, and believe that each person's well-being is inextricably linked to that of society. The group in the zone of negative factor values (three clusters) is called "social individualists": they hold a negative attitude to patriotism as a social value and are not ready to share the fruits of their labour with their country. The third, intermediate group is called "socially undecided": its members lie in the zone of neutral factor values and show no pronounced positive or negative attitude. Using correlation analysis, a list of values related to patriotism was formed, half of which are assessed sharply negatively and half positively by "social individualists". It is assumed that youth-policy mechanisms aimed at raising patriotism and built on positively assessed values will be more effective in forming patriotism among students who currently reject it — the author's next research task.

Author's English translation of the article published in Russian: Sociological Science and Social Practice (Sotsiologicheskaya nauka i sotsial'naya praktika), 2025, vol. 13, no. 1, pp. 142–169. DOI: 10.19181/snsp.2025.13.1.7. The Russian original is the version of record. Archived translation: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21610446

articles.title: NITR SOVEREIGN WEALTH FUNDS AND NON-DEPRECIATING INVESTMENT GROWTH
articles.authors: Timothy Kessler
articles.abstract:
Sovereign wealth funds, (SWFs) are increasingly used by diverse countries to support large-scale economic development. However, limited evidence exists regarding these national outcomes. I investigate Norway and Singapore, the only open high-income (HI) economies with SWF assets exceeding GDP. Multi-model synthetic control methods (SCMs) with negative control outcomes estimate a treatment effect of $27,716 USD, $24,126 PPP, and $15,804 USD investment (2021 GDP per capita) by Norway’s Government Pension Fund (1995-2023). SCMs estimate a structural economic output acceleration of $19,124 US$, $37,006 PPP, and $21,594 USD investment per capita in Singapore attributable to its National Investment Income (NII) SWF investment (2003-2003). GPF and NII increased gross domestic savings % of GDP 8.3%, 26.4% by ratio in Norway, and 10.24%, 25.2% by ratio in Singapore.
 I identify a specific model of SWF investment in these economies “NITR,” (National-Investment Transfer-Return”), in terms of the Solow Model. Under NITR, surplus output is withheld from automatic economic capital that would typically depreciate. A majority is transferred to SWF asset growth, while a smaller share is allocated to investment capital expansion. The greater surplus value of SWF reserves withheld from capital are used to offset net national depreciation equivalent to that created by new investment output. This mechanism produced Norway and Singapore’s unique pattern of non-asymptotic late-stage output and savings rate growth, adjusted for external trade pathways. Since sources of SWF savings are heterogenous, including mandated household savings in low-income countries, modified NITR SWFs could support output and savings growth in diverse policy environments.

articles.title: Social and Professional Orientations of Student Youth as a Foundation for Building the Human Resource Potential in Public Authorities (Author's English Translation)
articles.authors: Inna Gazieva
articles.abstract:
The article presents an analysis of the results of a sociological survey conducted among students at the Russian Presidential Academy of National Economy and Public Administration (N=1943). Based on these findings, the human resource potential of public authorities is described, and conclusions are drawn about the influence of the professional environment on the formation of the social and professional orientations of future civil servants during their studies at the university.

The study shows that significant predictors of an orientation towards employment in government organizations include values such as responsibility for the country's future, a desire for a high social status, and the preservation of the nation's historical memory. The most crucial factor for municipal service is a desire to benefit the society. The author also investigated the impact of socio-demographic and other factors on the desire to pursue a career in public service. Students at the Presidential Academy who study in regional areas are predominantly male and demonstrate a negative attitude towards remote working, and are more likely to be interested in working for public authorities.

Author's English translation of the article published in Russian: Public Administration (Gosudarstvennaya sluzhba), 2025, vol. 27, no. 4, pp. 79–87. EDN: DHQCIH. The Russian original is the version of record. Archived translation: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21610452
